text:
alice: FYI p95/p99 spike observed across streaming routes, starting ~17:02 UTC. Dashboard shows p95 jumping from ~120ms -> 430ms and p99 from ~480ms -> 2.1s. Many streaming sessions report stalls at ~100 tokens.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-20260315-47: Streaming tail latency spike / cache miss surge (automated alert).
ben: seeing a big change in prefix cache hitrate for the last hour — global hit rate down from 91% to 29%. Prefetch queue depth spiking. Logs show a lot of "prefix-mismatch" warnings from prefixhash v3 rollout.
chandra: confirmed. correlation matrix shows new prefix-hash salt deployed in canary at 16:58 UTC and then promoted. Crash window aligns.
devon: is the rollout the salted-prefix change from today? I flagged it in the release notes but didn’t expect this magnitude.
alice: yes, release id r20260315-saltv2. Looks like the salt permutation changed keyspace distribution and invalidated many cached prefixes.
ben: sample log snippet: ```WARN prefix_cache: key=kv:pref:0x7fa1 mismatch expected=0x9c3 got=0x4b2```
chandra: impact: streaming route p99 up, token throughput down ~38% on dedicated pools, increased CPU due to excessive backend calls. Customer visible for ~5 customers on dedicated capacity (escalating).
oncall: I’m taking on-call. starting mitigation checklist.
devon: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) pause salted-prefix rollout (rollback to previous salt) 2) enable aggressive cache-warm for top 100k prefixes 3) temporarily relax prefetch backpressure thresholds to allow faster warming 4) enable fallback-serving to non-prefetch path for critical customers. Any objections?
alice: +1 to pause/rollback. I can trigger rollback to salt v1 now if we want to minimize churn.
ben: while rollback is in progress, we should also throttle rate of re-request storms from prefetch workers — they’re amplifying load. Suggest scaling prefetch workers down to 30% and enable exponential backoff in retriers.
chandra: running a small script to compute top prefixes impacted and push warm requests. Command I’ll run: ```/opt/tools/prefetch_warm --prefix-list /tmp/top-prefixes-100k.txt --concurrency 200```
oncall: please post the prefetch job id when started. Also enabling route-fallback for customers with SLOs is critical — how many are on fallback?
alice: enabling fallback policies for tenants tagged "sla-critical" now (policy id pf-20260315-01).
ezra-cs: (ezra-cs) Notified CS about 5 affected enterprise accounts. Drafting customer message: "We are investigating a latency issue affecting streaming. We have mitigation in progress and will follow up with ETA"
ben: rollback started — coordinator reports rollback job j-9981 initiated, estimated 3m to propagate to all gateway pools.
chandra: prefetch warm job started id warm-772, concurrency 200, will report progress. Initial warm batch shows hitrate for warmed prefixes ~94% after boot requests.
devon: scaling prefetch workers down to 30% now and toggling retrier backoff. Patch applied to prefetch-config: ```max_workers=60
retry_base_ms=200
retry_multiplier=2```
oncall: monitoring: p95 trending down to ~180ms, p99 to ~620ms. Streaming stall count (sessions stalled >5s) dropping from 340 -> 48 in last 3m.
alice: rollback completed across gateways at 17:08 UTC according to deploybot. Confirming prefixhash salt reverted to v1.
ben: cache-hit telemetry: global hit rate climbed to 76% after warmers; still below baseline but much improved.
chandra: I'm seeing some lingering hotshard pressure — one shard experienced pagefaults during warm. Increasing io buffers and triggering shard rebalancer for that pool.
oncall: customer impact summary to log: 5 enterprise customers saw degraded streaming UX (stalls and reconnects). Public hosted customers ~0.8% requests saw elevated tail latency. No data loss.
ezra-cs: sent initial customer notice. Will follow up with a post-incident summary and affected window.
devon: follow-ups: 1) add canary gating for prefix-salt changes (must validate hitrate delta on canary for 30m before promotion) 2) add automatic rollback threshold if cache hitrate drops >15% 3) improve prefetch backpressure to avoid re-request amplification 4) run an experiment to precompute salted mapping for top prefixes.
alice: created follow-up tickets: TKT-5021 (canary gating), TKT-5022 (auto-rollback trigger), TKT-5023 (prefetch backpressure fix), TKT-5024 (hot-prefix precompute).
chandra: warm job finished: warm-772 completed, final warmed set size 103k, post-warm global hit=88%. Will handoff remaining ops to devon.
oncall: handing off to devon for next 8h on-call carry. Please summarize state: rollback done, warm complete, prefetch scaled down, fallback enabled for SLA customers, follow-ups created.
devon: taking over. I’ll keep an eye on p99 < 700ms target and ensure shard rebalance completes. If anything regresses, page-eng to wake.
alice: adding incident note in tracker and tagging "customer-impact". Closing this Slack thread, will open postmortem doc once we have a timeline and root cause analysis. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-47 marked resolved by alice at 17:21 UTC.
ben: quick postmortem notes: root cause = un-gated prefix-salt promotion -> cache invalidation wave -> prefetch amplification. Mitigation = rollback + warm + prefetch throttling + customer fallback.
ezra-cs: CS follow-up scheduled, will attach impact table and customers contacted."
